prompt: A $13$-ft ladder leans against a wall with its foot $5$ ft from the base of the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach, in feet?
hint: The ladder is the hypotenuse — it is the longest side, leaning across from the right angle where wall meets ground.

hints.text: The ladder is the hypotenuse — it is the longest side, leaning across from the right angle where wall meets ground.
Here $c = 13$ and one leg is $5$: solve $5^2 + b^2 = 13^2$.

explanation: The wall and ground form the right angle, so the ladder is the hypotenuse: $c = 13$.
Subtract: $b^2 = 144$, so the ladder reaches $b = 12$ ft up the wall.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why subtract instead of add
steps: When you are hunting the hypotenuse you add the squares; when the hypotenuse is already known you subtract.
Sanity check: $12$ is shorter than the $13$-ft ladder, which is exactly what a leaning ladder should do.
